statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low and well below the block threshold after an orderly two-sided U.S. session, while Stress remains elevated ahead of the stacked 26 August releases and the NVIDIA report that follows the next close.
recommendation: The 25 August cash session closed with NQ futures near 29,270, up 0.56%, having absorbed rather than extended the 29,157 pullback low inside a 269-point range. VIX finished near 14.89, both key Treasury yields eased and WTI fell more than 5% on reduced U.S.-Iran escalation risk, which describes functioning rather than failing mean reversion, so the mapped state remains EA_ON. A narrow danger window is marked from the 26 August 12:30Z PCE, GDP and durable-goods stack through 15:00Z, where the conditional forecast Tail reaches the watch band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes an orderly two-sided session with volatility, yields and crude all lower; risk stays concentrated on Wednesday's PCE, GDP and NVIDIA stack
body: NQ futures settled near 29,270, about +0.56% on the session, inside a 29,157-29,426 range roughly 269 points wide, closing about 113 points above the low and 156 below the high. The decisive structural observation is that the intraday pullback was absorbed and reversed rather than failing: the tape kept an upward bias but stayed clearly two-sided, and mean reversion worked throughout. The U.S. cash indices confirm the tone without any sign of one-way structure, with the S&P 500 up about 0.32%, the Dow up about 0.30%, the Nasdaq Composite up about 0.66% and the Russell 2000 up about 0.50%. Cross-assets support that read instead of amplifying it. VIX closed near 14.89, down about 6% with a 14.77-15.95 range, the 10-year yield eased roughly seven basis points to about 4.63% and the 2-year about five basis points to 4.18%, while WTI fell more than 5% to near $80.5 and Brent to about $86.4 after investors judged the latest U.S. sanctions on Iran to be economic pressure rather than a supply shock. Leadership was narrow but constructive: the semiconductor group was firm with AMD up about 4.9%, Micron near 2.5%, NVIDIA near 2.1% and six of seven names higher, while the megacap group split evenly four to four as Apple, Amazon, Alphabet and Broadcom finished lower. That split is a conviction-reducing rather than a Tail-amplifying condition. Today's macro was soft without being disorderly: Conference Board consumer confidence printed 89.4 against 90.2 expected, the weakest since January, with the expectations index down to 68.2, and July new home sales fell 10.5% month over month to 607,000. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on roughly $20 billion of U.S. goods, at rates of 15%, 25% and 50% effective 8 September, remain a live policy thread that has not produced index-level one-way structure. Tail is set at 11: there is no persistent directional efficiency, no sequence of failed retracements and no cluster of aligned amplifiers, and the cash close removes the intraday continuation channel. Stress is 45 because the 26 August stack is genuinely heavy, combining the July PCE and core PCE price indices, the second GDP estimate, durable goods and personal income and outlays at 12:30Z with the NVIDIA report after the following close. Confidence is 88: closing index and futures levels, the day range, VIX, both key yields, crude, breadth, megacap and semiconductor tone, the verified event calendar and fresh shared delayed cross-asset context were all available and broadly consistent.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the assessment never left the low-to-watch Tail band. Tail sat between 7 and 12 through the 24 August U.S. evening and the Asian session under normal and mixed modes, then built steadily from 04:00Z on 25 August as a trend-up bias developed, reaching 15 to 17 by the European morning. Between 09:00Z and 13:00Z the reading held the 20-21 watch band across the European session, the U.S. pre-market and the first cash hour, the only stretch of the window mapped to yellow. From 14:00Z the mode reverted to mixed as the U.S. session produced two-way trade rather than continuation, and Tail unwound steadily to 12 by 18:00Z and held there into the close. Stress stayed in the elevated 42-51 band throughout, and Confidence held between 84 and 88, so the de-escalation reflects observed structure rather than thinning evidence.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours divide into three phases. The 25 August U.S. evening and the overnight Asian and early European stretch carry no scheduled U.S. release, and conditional Tail sits at the low end, 10 to 13, on the working assumption of a contained range across the futures maintenance break, the Tokyo open and the European handover. The second phase is the European morning and U.S. pre-market, where conditional Tail drifts from 13 to 17 as positioning into the release stack builds and ranges are assumed to compress rather than trend. The third phase is the 26 August data stack: conditional Tail steps into the watch band at 23 for the 12:00Z hour containing the 12:30Z PCE, GDP, durable-goods and personal-income releases, peaks at 24 for the 13:00Z hour where post-release discovery meets the U.S. cash open, then eases to 21 and back below the watch band from 15:00Z as the repricing is assumed to be absorbed. Stress follows a similar arc, peaking at 63. Confidence declines from 88 to 72 across the window, which is the normal decay of forecast evidence quality with distance. NVIDIA reports after the 26 August close, just outside this horizon, so the final hours reflect positioning into that catalyst rather than the catalyst itself.
